docs.title: QuickLook 3
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation for QuickLook 3—a modern, high-performance Python/Qt-based application designed for viewing integral field spectroscopy (IFU) data.

This tool is a replacement for the legacy IDL qlook2 GUI for viewing and analyzing FITS data originally built for the OSIRIS instrument at the Keck Observatory. While QuickLook 3 is optimized for OSIRIS data, it works seamlessly with most IFU instruments including JWST NIRSpec IFU and Gemini NIFS.

docs.title: 🚀 Downloads (Version v3.1.0)

Download the standalone compiled application for your operating system below. No Python installation is required.

View all releases and source code on GitHub

macOS Installation Note

Because this is an open-source tool, it is not signed with a paid Apple Developer certificate. When you first open the app, macOS may block it and display a warning that the app "cannot be opened" or "is from an unidentified developer".

How to open the app:

  1. The Right-Click Method (Easiest): Instead of double-clicking, Right-click (or Control-click) on QuickLook3.app and select Open. You will get a similar warning dialog, but this one will have an Open button.
  2. The Settings Method: Double-click the app. When it fails, open your Mac's System Settings ➔ Privacy & Security. Scroll down, and you will see a message that QuickLook 3 was blocked. Click Open Anyway.
  3. The Terminal Method: If macOS falsely claims the app is "damaged and should be moved to the trash", open your Terminal and remove the quarantine attribute by running: 
    xattr -cr /path/to/QuickLook3.app

Launching from the terminal, and opening FITS files from Finder

After dragging QuickLook3.app to your Applications folder, choose Help ➔ Install 'quicklook3' Command Line Tool... to get a quicklook3 command on your PATH:

quicklook3 cube.fits --collapse-range 100 200

The dialog shows exactly where the command will be installed and how to remove it again (rm the one file it creates), and nothing is written until you agree.

The bundle also registers as a viewer for .fits, .fit, .fts and .fz, so QuickLook 3 shows up in Finder's Open With menu.

One ordering note: open the app from Finder at least once (or run the xattr -cr command above) before using quicklook3. macOS kills a freshly downloaded, quarantined app with no message when it is started from a shell. See the Command Line Guide for details.

docs.title: ✨ Key Features
docs.text:
• High-Performance Rendering: Built on PySide6 and pyqtgraph for efficient, hardware-accelerated visualization of large FITS data cubes.
  • IFU Data Cube Visualization: View FITS cubes interactively. Extract depth spectra from specific spatial pixels.
  • Z-Axis Collapsing: Collapse 3D ranges into 2D display slices using Median, Mean, or Sum algorithms on the fly.
  • Astronomical Coordinates: Integrates WCS pixel-to-world (RA/Dec) coordinate translations at your mouse pointer.
  • Advanced Scaling: Includes interactive Linear, Logarithmic, Square Root, AsinH, and Histogram Equalization scaling.
  • Analysis Tools: Features built-in region cuts (horizontal, vertical, arbitrary lines), SNR estimates, Encircled Energy plots, 2D Peak Fitting, and Catalog Plotting.
  • ds9-Style Regions: Draw circles, boxes, arrows and text over the image, edit them from a properties dialog or a table, and save or load them as readable YAML or ds9 .reg files.
  • Several Cubes at Once: Open as many windows as you like (File ➔ New Window, or one per file on the command line). Each window has its own scaling, colormap and analysis tools, so two cubes can be compared side by side.
  • Live File Polling: Monitor a directory for incoming data files and automatically load them in real-time.

docs.title: 🛠️ Developer Installation
docs.text:
If you prefer to run the application using Python instead of the compiled binaries, PyQL3 manages its dependencies using uv.

# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/astrodatalab/pyql3.git
cd pyql3

# 2. Run with uv (auto-installs all dependencies)
uv run python main.py

docs.title: FitsReader
docs.text:
Wrapper class for handling FITS file reading and header management.

Source code in pyql3/core/fits_reader.py 
class FitsReader:
    """Wrapper class for handling FITS file reading and header management."""
    def __init__(self, filepath=None):
        self.filepath = filepath
        self.hdul = None
        self.data = None
        self.header = None
        self.image_extensions = []
        self._file_signature = None
        self._scaling = {}

        if filepath:
            self.load(filepath)

    @staticmethod
    def _stat_signature(filepath):
        """Identity of the bytes on disk. Any change here means we must reopen."""
        try:
            st = os.stat(filepath)
        except OSError:
            return None
        return (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size, st.st_ino)

    def load(self, filepath, ext=None, force=False, require_data=False):
        """Loads a FITS file and its primary data/header.

        The HDUList is reopened whenever the file on disk differs from the one we hold
        open — *including* when the path is unchanged. An instrument or DRP that rewrites
        a path in place was previously served the cached copy forever (B5). Reuse is kept
        for the byte-identical case so that switching extensions stays cheap and does not
        throw away header edits that have not been saved yet. `force=True` reopens
        regardless, for an explicit "reload from disk".

        All or nothing: the new file is opened and the chosen extension's data read before
        anything here is replaced, so if any of that raises, the reader still holds the
        file it held before, open (R12). A frame still being copied fails in the data
        read, and the window that displays the old file goes on acting on it.

        `require_data=True` raises `NoImageData`, also before anything is replaced, when
        the chosen extension holds no 2-D or 3-D image.
        """
        if not os.path.exists(filepath):
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"FITS file not found: {filepath}")

        signature = self._stat_signature(filepath)
        stale = (self.hdul is None
                 or self.filepath != filepath
                 or signature is None
                 or signature != self._file_signature)
        if force or stale:
            # memmap=False: reading through a mapping of a file the DRP is rewriting under
            # us yields undefined data (and can SIGBUS if it shrinks), and writeto() back
            # to the same path can fail while the mapping is open.
            hdul = fits.open(filepath, memmap=False)
        else:
            hdul = self.hdul

        try:
            # Before any data is read; see `_integer_scaling_of`.
            scaling = self._scaling if hdul is self.hdul else _integer_scaling_of(hdul)
            image_extensions = self._image_extensions_of(hdul)
            if ext is not None:
                data = hdul[ext].data
            elif image_extensions:
                ext = image_extensions[0][0]
                data = hdul[ext].data
            else:
                ext, data = 0, None
            header = hdul[ext].header if data is not None else hdul[0].header
            # The viewer shows only 2-D and 3-D arrays. An extension asked for by number
            # need not be displayable: a 1-D or 4-D image, or a table, whose FITS_rec is 1-D.
            if require_data and (data is None or data.ndim not in (2, 3)):
                raise NoImageData(f"No displayable image in {os.path.basename(filepath)}")
        except BaseException:
            if hdul is not self.hdul:
                hdul.close()
            raise

        if hdul is not self.hdul:
            self.close()
            self.hdul = hdul
            self._file_signature = signature
            self._scaling = scaling
        self.filepath = filepath
        self.image_extensions = image_extensions
        self.current_ext = ext
        self.data = data
        # With no displayable image, `data` deliberately stays None so callers can tell
        # "nothing to show" from "here is your image", and the primary header is published
        # so the file can be inspected.
        #
        # This used to substitute np.zeros((10, 10)) with an empty Header. That made
        # `data` never None, which silently disabled every `if data is None` guard in the
        # application: a FITS carrying no image HDU was displayed as a black 10x10
        # square, titled with the filename and added to Recent Files, indistinguishable
        # from a real observation of an empty field.
        self.header = header

    def reference_header(self):
        """The header to take the WCS and the integration time from when the current
        extension's own header lacks them (R25), or None when it has both.

        A JWST ERR or DQ extension has no WCS cards, and an OSIRIS noise or quality extension
        has an empty header. When the WCS is missing, the reference is the first other image
        extension with the same data shape whose header has a celestial or spectral axis (SCI
        in a JWST file, the primary in an OSIRIS file), else the primary header. When only the
        integration time is missing, it is the primary header, where OSIRIS and NIFS keep it.
        None when the reference would be the current extension itself.

        Only headers are read, so no other extension's data is pulled into memory. The viewer
        decides what it uses from the reference: it does not apply a WCS with fewer axes than
        the data (a NIFS primary's WCS is the 2-D detector frame's), and takes `BUNIT` and the
        integration time from it only when it is the primary header and the data are not
        integers (`header_info.data_keywords`). So an extension lacking both, whose reference
        is the sibling with the WCS (JWST DQ beside SCI), borrows the WCS and no unit.
        """
        header = self.header
        if self.hdul is None or header is None or self.data is None:
            return None
        has_wcs = _has_world_axes(header)
        if has_wcs and states_integration_time(header):
            return None
        if not has_wcs:
            shape = _header_shape(header)
            for idx, _name in self.image_extensions:
                candidate = self.hdul[idx].header
                if (idx != self.current_ext and _header_shape(candidate) == shape
                        and _has_world_axes(candidate)):
                    return candidate
        if self.current_ext == 0:
            return None
        return self.hdul[0].header

    def holds_current_copy(self, path):
        """True if `path` is the file this reader holds and it is unchanged on disk.

        After `save()` the reader has reopened the file it wrote, so this is true of the
        reader's own save until something else changes the file. A watched directory
        announces that save as a changed file (R70), naming it through the watch
        directory, which need not be spelled the way the file was opened -- hence the
        canonical comparison, as the poller's `_watch_key` makes.
        """
        if self.filepath is None or self._file_signature is None:
            return False
        if _canonical(path) != _canonical(self.filepath):
            return False
        return self._stat_signature(path) == self._file_signature

    def load_from_memory(self, data, header):
        """Hold `data` as a one-HDU file with no path, such as an Arithmetic result.

        The header kept is the HDU's own, not the caller's: `PrimaryHDU` normalises a copy
        (BITPIX from the data's type, BZERO and BSCALE dropped for float data), and keeping
        the caller's object as well left two headers that disagreed, of which the Header
        Editor edited one and Save wrote the other (R23).
        """
        if self.hdul:
            self.hdul.close()

        if header is not None and data is not None and np.asarray(data).dtype.kind == 'f':
            # FITS defines BLANK for integer data only, and an integer operand's header has
            # one. Removed from a copy before the HDU is built, which otherwise warns.
            header = header.copy()
            header.remove('BLANK', ignore_missing=True, remove_all=True)
        hdu = fits.PrimaryHDU(data=data, header=header)
        self.hdul = fits.HDUList([hdu])
        self.filepath = None
        self._file_signature = None
        self._scaling = {}
        self.current_ext = 0
        self.data = data
        self.header = hdu.header
        self.image_extensions = self.get_image_extensions()


    def get_all_extensions(self):
        extensions = []
        if self.hdul:
            for idx, hdu in enumerate(self.hdul):
                name = hdu.name if hdu.name else f"EXT {idx}"
                extensions.append((idx, name))
        elif self.header is not None:
            extensions.append((0, "PRIMARY"))
        return extensions

    @staticmethod
    def _is_displayable(hdu):
        """Whether an HDU holds an image the viewer can actually show.

        An image HDU with two or three axes: the viewer shows nothing else, so a 1-D or 4-D
        image is neither offered in the Extension combo nor picked by default, and a file whose
        primary is 4-D opens its 3-D SCI extension.

        Header-only on purpose: touching `hdu.data` here would pull every extension of a
        multi-extension file into memory now that `memmap` is off, and `data is not None`
        is also the wrong question — a `BINTABLE` answers yes (B6).
        """
        if not getattr(hdu, 'is_image', False):
            return False
        try:
            return int(hdu.header.get('NAXIS', 0)) in (2, 3)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return False

    def get_image_extensions(self):
        """The extensions the viewer can display.

        The single definition of "displayable", shared with `load()` — the two used to
        disagree, so the Extension combo offered table HDUs that silently left the previous
        image on screen while `data`/`header` switched to the table underneath (B6).
        """
        return self._image_extensions_of(self.hdul)

    @classmethod
    def _image_extensions_of(cls, hdul):
        """`get_image_extensions()` for a given HDUList, which `load()` needs before it
        has replaced `self.hdul`."""
        extensions = []
        if hdul:
            for idx, hdu in enumerate(hdul):
                if not cls._is_displayable(hdu):
                    continue
                name = hdu.name if hdu.name else f"EXT {idx}"
                if name == "PRIMARY" and idx != 0:
                    name = f"EXT {idx}"
                extensions.append((idx, name))
        return extensions

    def get_data(self):
        return self.data

    def get_header(self, ext=None):
        if ext is not None and self.hdul and 0 <= ext < len(self.hdul):
            return self.hdul[ext].header
        return self.header

    #: Keywords that describe the physical layout of the file rather than the
    #: observation. Editing them is either destructive or futile:
    #:
    #:   SIMPLE = F marks the file as non-conforming, and the primary HDU then stops
    #:   being recognised as an image — save() overwrites in place, so one keystroke
    #:   in the Header Editor could make a science file unreadable.
    #:
    #:   NAXIS/NAXISn/BITPIX and friends are regenerated by astropy from the data
    #:   array on write, so an edit silently reverts, which merely confuses.
    #:
    #: Either way the viewer should not be the tool that does it.
    PROTECTED_KEYWORDS = frozenset({
        'SIMPLE', 'XTENSION', 'BITPIX', 'NAXIS', 'END', 'EXTEND', 'PCOUNT', 'GCOUNT',
        'TFIELDS',
    })

    #: Cards that hold free text and no comment field.
    COMMENTARY_KEYWORDS = frozenset({'', 'COMMENT', 'HISTORY'})

    @classmethod
    def is_protected_keyword(cls, keyword):
        """True for structural keywords, including the NAXISn / TFORMn families."""
        name = str(keyword).strip().upper()
        if name in cls.PROTECTED_KEYWORDS:
            return True
        for prefix in ('NAXIS', 'TFORM', 'TBCOL'):
            if name.startswith(prefix) and name[len(prefix):].isdigit():
                return True
        return False

    def _keeps_keyword(self, keyword, ext):
        """True if `keyword` of extension `ext` (None: the current one) may not be edited:
        a structural keyword, or BSCALE, BZERO or BLANK of an HDU whose integers `save()`
        writes back with the file's own scaling cards (`_integer_scaling_of`). An edit to those
        would be replaced by the recorded cards, so it is refused rather than lost."""
        if self.is_protected_keyword(keyword):
            return True
        index = self.current_ext if ext is None else ext
        return (str(keyword).strip().upper() in ('BSCALE', 'BZERO', 'BLANK')
                and index in self._scaling)

    def update_header_card(self, keyword, value, comment=None, ext=None):
        """Update or add a header card. Returns False if the keyword may not be edited
        (`_keeps_keyword`)."""
        if self._keeps_keyword(keyword, ext):
            return False

        hdr = self.get_header(ext=ext)
        if hdr is None:
            return False
        if comment is not None:
            hdr[keyword] = (value, comment)
        else:
            hdr[keyword] = value
        return True

    def update_header_card_at(self, index, value, comment=None, ext=None):
        """Set the value, and the comment if given, of the card at position `index`.

        By position, because a keyword names only its first card: writing a second FILTER
        card by name overwrote the first (R42). A COMMENT, HISTORY or blank card has no
        comment field, so only its text is set. Returns False, writing nothing, for a
        keyword that may not be edited (`_keeps_keyword`).
        """
        hdr = self.get_header(ext=ext)
        if hdr is None:
            return False
        card = hdr.cards[index]
        if self._keeps_keyword(card.keyword, ext):
            return False
        if card.keyword in self.COMMENTARY_KEYWORDS:
            hdr[index] = value
        elif comment is not None:
            hdr[index] = (value, comment)
        else:
            hdr[index] = value
        return True

    def _stored_integers(self):
        """`{HDU index: integers}` for the HDUs in `_scaling`, read from the file as stored.

        Exactly what the file holds. Rebuilding the integers from astropy's floats is not
        exact: for BITPIX 8 and 16 those are float32, which cannot hold every
        `stored * BSCALE + BZERO` (with BSCALE 1e-4 and BZERO 2000, one pixel in six moved one
        step), and scaled BITPIX 64 loses bits even in float64. Valid because the viewer
        never changes pixel data, only headers. Tile-compressed HDUs are read exactly too.
        Empty when the file on disk is no longer the one that was read.
        """
        if (not self._scaling or self.filepath is None
                or self._stat_signature(self.filepath) != self._file_signature):
            return {}
        stored = {}
        with fits.open(self.filepath, memmap=False, do_not_scale_image_data=True) as raw:
            for idx in self._scaling:
                if raw[idx].data is not None:
                    stored[idx] = np.array(raw[idx].data)
        return stored

    def save(self, output_filepath=None):
        """Write the in-memory HDUList out, overwriting the target if it exists.

        Saving over the file we currently have open needs care on Windows: a file with an
        open handle cannot be deleted or replaced, and astropy implements `overwrite=True`
        as `os.remove()` followed by a fresh create. That made the Header Editor's
        "save directly to file" fail with `PermissionError: [WinError 32]`.

        So: pull every HDU into memory, release the OS handle, write to a sibling temp file
        and swap it in with `os.replace()` (atomic on both platforms, and it never leaves a
        half-written file where the original was). Then reopen so our state matches disk.
        """
        if self.hdul is None:
            raise ValueError("No FITS file loaded.")

        save_path = output_filepath or self.filepath
        if not save_path:
            raise ValueError("No output path given and no current file path is known.")

        hdul = self.hdul

        # Materialise before dropping the handle: with memmap off these become real arrays
        # that stay valid after close(), which lazily-loaded HDUs would not.
        for hdu in hdul:
            _ = hdu.data

        # Integers that astropy read as floats go back as the file stores them (R71). Checked
        # and built before anything is closed or written, so a refusal leaves the reader and
        # the file as they were.
        stored = self._stored_integers()
        for idx, hdu in enumerate(hdul):
            if (_reads_as_floats(hdu, self._scaling.get(idx))
                    and (idx not in stored or stored[idx].shape != hdu.data.shape)):
                # The integers can only be read from the file that was opened. Rebuilding
                # them from astropy's floats moves values (see `_stored_integers`), and an
                # in-place save would also overwrite the newer file with this older content.
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{os.path.basename(self.filepath or '')} changed on disk since it was "
                    "opened, so its integer data cannot be written back exactly as the file "
                    "stores them. Nothing was saved. Reopen the file and make the change "
                    "again.")
        to_write = fits.HDUList([
            _encoded_for_writing(hdu, self._scaling.get(idx), stored.get(idx))
            for idx, hdu in enumerate(hdul)])

        try:
            hdul.close()
        except Exception:
            pass

        # Capture the target's permissions before it is replaced. mkstemp creates 0600
        # by design, and os.replace carries the temp file's mode onto the destination,
        # so saving a group-shared file used to silently drop it to owner-only and lock
        # collaborators out of a reduction directory. Nothing warned; they simply got
        # permission denied later.
        original_mode = None
        try:
            original_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(save_path).st_mode)
        except OSError:
            pass  # new file (Save As); fall back to the umask default below

        # Same directory as the target, so os.replace can never be cross-filesystem.
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(save_path)) or '.'
        # astropy picks gzip from the file name, so a `.gz` target needs a `.gz` temp name or
        # the swapped-in file is plain FITS under a compressed name.
        tmp_suffix = '.fits.gz' if save_path.lower().endswith('.gz') else '.fits'
        fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.pyql3_save_', suffix=tmp_suffix, dir=directory)
        os.close(fd)
        try:
            to_write.writeto(tmp_path, overwrite=True)
            os.chmod(tmp_path, original_mode if original_mode is not None
                     else _default_file_mode())
            os.replace(tmp_path, save_path)
        except BaseException:
            try:
                if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
                    os.remove(tmp_path)
            except OSError:
                pass
            raise

        # Our handle is gone and the bytes on disk have changed, so reopen from scratch.
        reopen_path = save_path if self.filepath in (None, save_path) else self.filepath
        ext = self.current_ext
        self.hdul = None
        self._file_signature = None
        if os.path.exists(reopen_path):
            self.load(reopen_path, ext=ext, force=True)


    def close(self):
        """Closes the FITS file handle."""
        if self.hdul is not None:
            self.hdul.close()
            self.hdul = None
            self.data = None
            self.header = None
            self._scaling = {}

def load(self, filepath, ext=None, force=False, require_data=False):
    """Loads a FITS file and its primary data/header.

    The HDUList is reopened whenever the file on disk differs from the one we hold
    open — *including* when the path is unchanged. An instrument or DRP that rewrites
    a path in place was previously served the cached copy forever (B5). Reuse is kept
    for the byte-identical case so that switching extensions stays cheap and does not
    throw away header edits that have not been saved yet. `force=True` reopens
    regardless, for an explicit "reload from disk".

    All or nothing: the new file is opened and the chosen extension's data read before
    anything here is replaced, so if any of that raises, the reader still holds the
    file it held before, open (R12). A frame still being copied fails in the data
    read, and the window that displays the old file goes on acting on it.

    `require_data=True` raises `NoImageData`, also before anything is replaced, when
    the chosen extension holds no 2-D or 3-D image.
    """
    if not os.path.exists(filepath):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"FITS file not found: {filepath}")

    signature = self._stat_signature(filepath)
    stale = (self.hdul is None
             or self.filepath != filepath
             or signature is None
             or signature != self._file_signature)
    if force or stale:
        # memmap=False: reading through a mapping of a file the DRP is rewriting under
        # us yields undefined data (and can SIGBUS if it shrinks), and writeto() back
        # to the same path can fail while the mapping is open.
        hdul = fits.open(filepath, memmap=False)
    else:
        hdul = self.hdul

    try:
        # Before any data is read; see `_integer_scaling_of`.
        scaling = self._scaling if hdul is self.hdul else _integer_scaling_of(hdul)
        image_extensions = self._image_extensions_of(hdul)
        if ext is not None:
            data = hdul[ext].data
        elif image_extensions:
            ext = image_extensions[0][0]
            data = hdul[ext].data
        else:
            ext, data = 0, None
        header = hdul[ext].header if data is not None else hdul[0].header
        # The viewer shows only 2-D and 3-D arrays. An extension asked for by number
        # need not be displayable: a 1-D or 4-D image, or a table, whose FITS_rec is 1-D.
        if require_data and (data is None or data.ndim not in (2, 3)):
            raise NoImageData(f"No displayable image in {os.path.basename(filepath)}")
    except BaseException:
        if hdul is not self.hdul:
            hdul.close()
        raise

    if hdul is not self.hdul:
        self.close()
        self.hdul = hdul
        self._file_signature = signature
        self._scaling = scaling
    self.filepath = filepath
    self.image_extensions = image_extensions
    self.current_ext = ext
    self.data = data
    # With no displayable image, `data` deliberately stays None so callers can tell
    # "nothing to show" from "here is your image", and the primary header is published
    # so the file can be inspected.
    #
    # This used to substitute np.zeros((10, 10)) with an empty Header. That made
    # `data` never None, which silently disabled every `if data is None` guard in the
    # application: a FITS carrying no image HDU was displayed as a black 10x10
    # square, titled with the filename and added to Recent Files, indistinguishable
    # from a real observation of an empty field.
    self.header = header

The header kept is the HDU's own, not the caller's: PrimaryHDU normalises a copy (BITPIX from the data's type, BZERO and BSCALE dropped for float data), and keeping the caller's object as well left two headers that disagreed, of which the Header Editor edited one and Save wrote the other (R23).

def load_from_memory(self, data, header):
    """Hold `data` as a one-HDU file with no path, such as an Arithmetic result.

    The header kept is the HDU's own, not the caller's: `PrimaryHDU` normalises a copy
    (BITPIX from the data's type, BZERO and BSCALE dropped for float data), and keeping
    the caller's object as well left two headers that disagreed, of which the Header
    Editor edited one and Save wrote the other (R23).
    """
    if self.hdul:
        self.hdul.close()

    if header is not None and data is not None and np.asarray(data).dtype.kind == 'f':
        # FITS defines BLANK for integer data only, and an integer operand's header has
        # one. Removed from a copy before the HDU is built, which otherwise warns.
        header = header.copy()
        header.remove('BLANK', ignore_missing=True, remove_all=True)
    hdu = fits.PrimaryHDU(data=data, header=header)
    self.hdul = fits.HDUList([hdu])
    self.filepath = None
    self._file_signature = None
    self._scaling = {}
    self.current_ext = 0
    self.data = data
    self.header = hdu.header
    self.image_extensions = self.get_image_extensions()

docs.text:
The header to take the WCS and the integration time from when the current extension's own header lacks them (R25), or None when it has both.

A JWST ERR or DQ extension has no WCS cards, and an OSIRIS noise or quality extension has an empty header. When the WCS is missing, the reference is the first other image extension with the same data shape whose header has a celestial or spectral axis (SCI in a JWST file, the primary in an OSIRIS file), else the primary header. When only the integration time is missing, it is the primary header, where OSIRIS and NIFS keep it. None when the reference would be the current extension itself.

Only headers are read, so no other extension's data is pulled into memory. The viewer decides what it uses from the reference: it does not apply a WCS with fewer axes than the data (a NIFS primary's WCS is the 2-D detector frame's), and takes BUNIT and the integration time from it only when it is the primary header and the data are not integers (header_info.data_keywords). So an extension lacking both, whose reference is the sibling with the WCS (JWST DQ beside SCI), borrows the WCS and no unit.

def reference_header(self):
    """The header to take the WCS and the integration time from when the current
    extension's own header lacks them (R25), or None when it has both.

    A JWST ERR or DQ extension has no WCS cards, and an OSIRIS noise or quality extension
    has an empty header. When the WCS is missing, the reference is the first other image
    extension with the same data shape whose header has a celestial or spectral axis (SCI
    in a JWST file, the primary in an OSIRIS file), else the primary header. When only the
    integration time is missing, it is the primary header, where OSIRIS and NIFS keep it.
    None when the reference would be the current extension itself.

    Only headers are read, so no other extension's data is pulled into memory. The viewer
    decides what it uses from the reference: it does not apply a WCS with fewer axes than
    the data (a NIFS primary's WCS is the 2-D detector frame's), and takes `BUNIT` and the
    integration time from it only when it is the primary header and the data are not
    integers (`header_info.data_keywords`). So an extension lacking both, whose reference
    is the sibling with the WCS (JWST DQ beside SCI), borrows the WCS and no unit.
    """
    header = self.header
    if self.hdul is None or header is None or self.data is None:
        return None
    has_wcs = _has_world_axes(header)
    if has_wcs and states_integration_time(header):
        return None
    if not has_wcs:
        shape = _header_shape(header)
        for idx, _name in self.image_extensions:
            candidate = self.hdul[idx].header
            if (idx != self.current_ext and _header_shape(candidate) == shape
                    and _has_world_axes(candidate)):
                return candidate
    if self.current_ext == 0:
        return None
    return self.hdul[0].header

Write the in-memory HDUList out, overwriting the target if it exists.

Saving over the file we currently have open needs care on Windows: a file with an open handle cannot be deleted or replaced, and astropy implements overwrite=True as os.remove() followed by a fresh create. That made the Header Editor's "save directly to file" fail with PermissionError: [WinError 32].

So: pull every HDU into memory, release the OS handle, write to a sibling temp file and swap it in with os.replace() (atomic on both platforms, and it never leaves a half-written file where the original was). Then reopen so our state matches disk.

def save(self, output_filepath=None):
    """Write the in-memory HDUList out, overwriting the target if it exists.

    Saving over the file we currently have open needs care on Windows: a file with an
    open handle cannot be deleted or replaced, and astropy implements `overwrite=True`
    as `os.remove()` followed by a fresh create. That made the Header Editor's
    "save directly to file" fail with `PermissionError: [WinError 32]`.

    So: pull every HDU into memory, release the OS handle, write to a sibling temp file
    and swap it in with `os.replace()` (atomic on both platforms, and it never leaves a
    half-written file where the original was). Then reopen so our state matches disk.
    """
    if self.hdul is None:
        raise ValueError("No FITS file loaded.")

    save_path = output_filepath or self.filepath
    if not save_path:
        raise ValueError("No output path given and no current file path is known.")

    hdul = self.hdul

    # Materialise before dropping the handle: with memmap off these become real arrays
    # that stay valid after close(), which lazily-loaded HDUs would not.
    for hdu in hdul:
        _ = hdu.data

    # Integers that astropy read as floats go back as the file stores them (R71). Checked
    # and built before anything is closed or written, so a refusal leaves the reader and
    # the file as they were.
    stored = self._stored_integers()
    for idx, hdu in enumerate(hdul):
        if (_reads_as_floats(hdu, self._scaling.get(idx))
                and (idx not in stored or stored[idx].shape != hdu.data.shape)):
            # The integers can only be read from the file that was opened. Rebuilding
            # them from astropy's floats moves values (see `_stored_integers`), and an
            # in-place save would also overwrite the newer file with this older content.
            raise ValueError(
                f"{os.path.basename(self.filepath or '')} changed on disk since it was "
                "opened, so its integer data cannot be written back exactly as the file "
                "stores them. Nothing was saved. Reopen the file and make the change "
                "again.")
    to_write = fits.HDUList([
        _encoded_for_writing(hdu, self._scaling.get(idx), stored.get(idx))
        for idx, hdu in enumerate(hdul)])

    try:
        hdul.close()
    except Exception:
        pass

    # Capture the target's permissions before it is replaced. mkstemp creates 0600
    # by design, and os.replace carries the temp file's mode onto the destination,
    # so saving a group-shared file used to silently drop it to owner-only and lock
    # collaborators out of a reduction directory. Nothing warned; they simply got
    # permission denied later.
    original_mode = None
    try:
        original_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(save_path).st_mode)
    except OSError:
        pass  # new file (Save As); fall back to the umask default below

    # Same directory as the target, so os.replace can never be cross-filesystem.
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(save_path)) or '.'
    # astropy picks gzip from the file name, so a `.gz` target needs a `.gz` temp name or
    # the swapped-in file is plain FITS under a compressed name.
    tmp_suffix = '.fits.gz' if save_path.lower().endswith('.gz') else '.fits'
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.pyql3_save_', suffix=tmp_suffix, dir=directory)
    os.close(fd)
    try:
        to_write.writeto(tmp_path, overwrite=True)
        os.chmod(tmp_path, original_mode if original_mode is not None
                 else _default_file_mode())
        os.replace(tmp_path, save_path)
    except BaseException:
        try:
            if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
                os.remove(tmp_path)
        except OSError:
            pass
        raise

    # Our handle is gone and the bytes on disk have changed, so reopen from scratch.
    reopen_path = save_path if self.filepath in (None, save_path) else self.filepath
    ext = self.current_ext
    self.hdul = None
    self._file_signature = None
    if os.path.exists(reopen_path):
        self.load(reopen_path, ext=ext, force=True)

def update_header_card(self, keyword, value, comment=None, ext=None):
    """Update or add a header card. Returns False if the keyword may not be edited
    (`_keeps_keyword`)."""
    if self._keeps_keyword(keyword, ext):
        return False

    hdr = self.get_header(ext=ext)
    if hdr is None:
        return False
    if comment is not None:
        hdr[keyword] = (value, comment)
    else:
        hdr[keyword] = value
    return True

def update_header_card_at(self, index, value, comment=None, ext=None):
    """Set the value, and the comment if given, of the card at position `index`.

    By position, because a keyword names only its first card: writing a second FILTER
    card by name overwrote the first (R42). A COMMENT, HISTORY or blank card has no
    comment field, so only its text is set. Returns False, writing nothing, for a
    keyword that may not be edited (`_keeps_keyword`).
    """
    hdr = self.get_header(ext=ext)
    if hdr is None:
        return False
    card = hdr.cards[index]
    if self._keeps_keyword(card.keyword, ext):
        return False
    if card.keyword in self.COMMENTARY_KEYWORDS:
        hdr[index] = value
    elif comment is not None:
        hdr[index] = (value, comment)
    else:
        hdr[index] = value
    return True

class ImageViewer(QWidget):
    request_depth_plot = Signal(object)
    request_gaussian_fit = Signal(object)
    #: A region was asked for from the right-click menu. Payload is `(kind, display pixel)`.
    request_new_region = Signal(str, object)
    #: Emitted when the displayed plane's geometry may have changed — a flip, a 90° rotation,
    #: a new axis mapping, new data — and also on a unit change, which redisplays through the
    #: same path. Anything drawn on top in stored coordinates has to be re-placed.
    #: Always emitted together with `plane_changed` and after it, so a tool that recomputes on
    #: `plane_changed` must not recompute again here unless it depends on the geometry alone.
    #: (The one exception is an unparsable Z Min/Max in Z Range mode, which draws no plane
    #: and so emits no `plane_changed`; see R84.)
    display_changed = Signal()
    #: Emitted once each time the values on screen change: a new channel, a boxcar or Z Range
    #: collapse, a flip, a 90° rotation or a unit change, new data. A view rotation does not
    #: emit it (see `view_rotation_changed`). Anything that shows or measures the current
    #: plane has to be recomputed. Every `display_changed` follows one; `plane_changed` alone
    #: means only the values changed (a slider step, a boxcar or Z Range change).
    plane_changed = Signal()
    #: Emitted by `apply_view_rotation` with the new angle in degrees. `set_data` emits it
    #: with 0.0 last, after the new plane's `plane_changed` and `display_changed`.
    view_rotation_changed = Signal(float)

    @property
    def transposed_data(self):
        """The cube or image in the axis order on screen; see AGENTS.md "Data state"."""
        return getattr(self, '_transposed_data', None)

    @transposed_data.setter
    def transposed_data(self, value):
        # Every assignment is new data as far as anything keyed on `data_generation` is
        # concerned, including an axis remapping of the same raw array.
        self._transposed_data = value
        self._data_generation = getattr(self, '_data_generation', 0) + 1
        self._drawn_collapse = None

    @property
    def data_generation(self):
        """A counter that changes whenever `transposed_data` is replaced.

        For caches of anything derived from the data: a new file, a new extension, a new axis
        mapping and `release_data` each change it, while a flip, a rotation or a unit change
        does not.
        """
        return getattr(self, '_data_generation', 0)

    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.layout = QVBoxLayout(self)
        self.layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)

        # Top: The Image View
        self.imv = pg.ImageView()
        self.imv.ui.histogram.hide()
        # The colorbar's ticks are positions in the rendered values; label them with the data
        # values those positions stand for (R65). `update_image_display` sets the inverse.
        self._colorbar_inverse = None
        self._colorbar_domain = None
        # pyqtgraph's automatic SI prefix would divide the ticks by a factor and put "(x1e-06)" in
        # the label, but these are data values already.
        self.imv.ui.histogram.axis.enableAutoSIPrefix(False)
        self.imv.ui.histogram.axis.tickStrings = self._colorbar_tick_strings
        self.imv.ui.roiBtn.hide()
        self.imv.ui.menuBtn.hide()
        self.imv.getView().setAspectLocked(True)
        self.imv.getView().invertY(False)
        self.imv.ui.roiPlot.setMinimumHeight(65)
        self.imv.ui.roiPlot.setMaximumHeight(85)
        self.layout.addWidget(self.imv, stretch=1)

        # Add region for highlighting stacked Z slices in the timeline
        self.z_range_region = pg.LinearRegionItem([0, 1], brush=(255, 255, 0, 120), pen=pg.mkPen((255, 255, 0, 200), width=3))
        self.z_range_region.setZValue(10)
        self.z_range_region.hide()
        self.z_range_region.sigRegionChangeFinished.connect(self.on_region_change_finished)
        self.imv.ui.roiPlot.addItem(self.z_range_region)
        self._updating_region = False

        self.imv.ui.roiPlot.scene().sigMouseClicked.connect(self.on_roi_plot_clicked)

        # Context menu setup on main image ViewBox
        self.last_right_click_pixel_pos = None
        view = self.imv.getView()
        view.scene().sigMouseClicked.connect(self.on_view_clicked)
        view.sigRangeChanged.connect(self.on_view_range_changed)
        if hasattr(view, 'menu') and view.menu is not None:
            view.menu.addSeparator()
            act_depth = view.menu.addAction("Depth Plot...")
            act_depth.triggered.connect(self.on_context_plot_depth)
            act_fit = view.menu.addAction("Gaussian Fit...")
            act_fit.triggered.connect(self.on_context_gaussian_fit)

            # Held on self, or PySide6 deletes the C++ menu with the first Python wrapper that
            # touches it, taking its actions with it (`BUGS.md` M11).
            self.new_region_menu = view.menu.addMenu("New Region")
            for label, kind in (("Circle", "circle"), ("Box", "box"),
                                ("Arrow", "arrow"), ("Text...", "text")):
                act = self.new_region_menu.addAction(label)
                act.triggered.connect(

        # Top axis for Wavelength

        self.top_axis.setStyle(showValues=True)
        self._original_tickStrings = self.top_axis.tickStrings
        self.top_axis.tickStrings = self._custom_tickStrings

        #: Wavelength unit), or None to take the header's. See set_wavelength_unit_override.

        self._spectral_stated_unit = None

        self.imv.timeLine.setPen(pg.mkPen('y', width=3))
        self.imv.timeLine.setHoverPen(pg.mkPen('y', width=5))

        self.set_colormap('cmc.oslo')

        # Data state
        self.raw_data = None
        self.transposed_data = None
        self.display_data = None
        self.wcs = None
        # Set by set_data: the extension's header, the header the WCS came from, and the
        # integration time and BUNIT, from either header (R25)
        self.header = None
        self.wcs_header = None
        self.data_keywords = None

        # Info Bar directly below image
        self.setup_info_panel()

        # Bottom: The Control Panels
        self.tabs = QTabWidget()
        self.layout.addWidget(self.tabs)

        self.tab_display = QWidget()
        self.display_layout = QVBoxLayout(self.tab_display)
        self.display_layout.setContentsMargins(4, 4, 4, 4)

        self.tab_advanced = QWidget()
        self.advanced_layout = QVBoxLayout(self.tab_advanced)
        self.advanced_layout.setContentsMargins(4, 4, 4, 4)

        self.tabs.addTab(self.tab_display, "Display")
        self.tabs.addTab(self.tab_advanced, "Advanced Data Cube")
        # Transforms state
        self.disp_as_dn = False
        self.rot_angle = 0
        self.view_rotation = 0.0
        self.flip = False
        self.pa_arrow = None
        # Set by set_data from data_keywords: the unit the values are in, and the DN/s -> Total
        # DN factor, None when the header states no integration time (R83)
        self.data_unit = data_unit(None)
        self._itime_coadds = None
        # Guards the slider <-> ImageView timeline sync (see on_imv_time_changed)
        self._syncing_slice = False
        # Exclusive drag handling; see begin_exclusive_drag
        self._drag_owner = None
        self._drag_handler_before = None
        self._drag_revoked_callback = None
        # True when the displayed plane has no finite pixels at all (see update_image_display)
        self._plane_all_invalid = False
        # Nonzero while apply_axis_mapping adjusts the slider, which redraws the plane

        self._plane_changed_held = 0

        self._planes_drawn = 0
        self._last_entry = None

        self.setup_zoom_contrast_panel()
        self.setup_extension_panel()
        self.setup_axis_panel()
        self.setup_z_axis_panel()

        self.tabs.currentChanged.connect(self.on_tab_changed)
        # Call it once after all layouts are fully constructed
        self.on_tab_changed(self.tabs.currentIndex())

        # Connect mouse movement and zoom scale
        self.proxy = pg.SignalProxy(self.imv.scene.sigMouseMoved, rateLimit=60, slot=self.mouse_moved)
        self.imv.timeLine.sigPositionChanged.connect(self.update_slice_info)

        # slider_slice is the single source of truth for the current z index; dragging the
        # pyqtgraph timeline has to write back to it or the labels, the pixel readout and

        self.imv.sigTimeChanged.connect(self.on_imv_time_changed)

        # eventFilter
        self.imv.installEventFilter(self)

        self.imv.playTimer.timeout.connect(self._after_playback_tick)

        self.region_layer = RegionLayer(self)

    def wavelength_unit(self):
        """The unit of the WCS's values on the spectral Z axis, or None when it is Unknown.

        The unit the user chose (`wavelength_unit_override`) when there is one, else the unit
        the file states. None means "Unknown" and is never replaced by a guess: the axis is
        labelled "Wavelength (Unknown)", shows the header's own numbers, and the line list is
        not matched against it. This is the one place the viewer and the tools ask for the unit;
        `wavelength_unit_label()` is the one place they ask how to label it.
        """
        if getattr(self, 'wcs_z_idx', None) is None:
            return None
        return self._spectral_values_unit()

    def _spectral_values_unit(self):
        """`wavelength_unit()` for the file's spectral axis, wherever it is displayed.

        A chosen unit describes the numbers the header writes. wcslib holds a stated `CUNIT`
        in SI (`nm` as `m`), so the chosen unit is scaled by `header_value_scale` to describe
        the WCS's values instead.
        """
        override = self.wavelength_unit_override
        if override is None:
            return self._spectral_header_unit
        if self._spectral_scale == 1.0:
            return override
        return u.CompositeUnit(self._spectral_scale, [override], [1])

    def _wavelength_display(self):
        """`(unit, chosen)`: the unit wavelengths are shown in, and whether the user chose it.

        The one decision behind `wavelength_display_unit` and `wavelength_unit_label`. The unit
        the user chose, in which the header's own numbers are shown; else µm when the header
        states a wavelength, frequency or energy unit; else None, when the header's numbers are
        shown as they are: Unknown, or a spectral axis that is not a wavelength (a velocity).
        """
        if self.wavelength_unit_override is not None:
            return self.wavelength_unit_override, True
        if in_microns(1.0, self._spectral_header_unit) is not None:
            return u.um, False
        return None, False

    def wavelength_display_unit(self):
        """The unit wavelengths are shown in, or None when the header's own numbers are shown
        (`_wavelength_display`)."""
        return self._wavelength_display()[0]

    def wavelength_unit_label(self):
        """The label for the numbers `displayed_wavelength` gives: "µm" for a unit the header
        states, "Å, set by you" for a unit the user chose, "Unknown" for neither."""
        unit, chosen = self._wavelength_display()
        if unit is None:
            header_unit = self._spectral_header_unit
            return UNKNOWN_UNIT if header_unit is None else unit_name(header_unit)
        return f"{unit_name(unit)}, set by you" if chosen else unit_name(unit)

    def _shows_stated_microns(self):
        """True when wavelengths are shown in µm because the header states their unit, and are
        written "2.2005 µm"; otherwise the label goes in parentheses, "(Å, set by you): 19968.7"."""
        unit, chosen = self._wavelength_display()
        return unit is not None and not chosen

    def header_wavelength_unit(self):
        """The spectral axis's unit as the header writes it (`stated_unit`), or None."""
        return self._spectral_stated_unit

    def displayed_wavelength(self, values):
        """WCS values on the spectral axis as the numbers shown, in `wavelength_display_unit()`.

        The values unchanged when the unit is Unknown, and None when they are not wavelengths.
        Accepts a number or an array.
        """
        unit = self._spectral_values_unit()
        if unit is None:
            return values
        target = self.wavelength_display_unit()
        if target is None:
            return None
        try:
            return (np.asarray(values, dtype=float) * unit).to_value(
                target, equivalencies=u.spectral())
        except u.UnitConversionError:
            return None

    def set_wavelength_unit_override(self, unit):
        """Read the spectral axis's numbers in `unit` (an astropy unit), or as the header
        states them when `unit` is None.

        The choice is the window's, and is kept across loads so that successive frames from one
        instrument keep it. A load whose header states a unit clears it, unless the choice was
        made over that same stated unit (`_set_spectral_axis`). Redraws the slice label and the
        timeline's wavelength axis; the Depth Plot, which sets it, redraws itself.
        """
        self.wavelength_unit_override = unit
        self._override_over_unit = self._spectral_stated_unit if unit is not None else None
        self._sync_timeline_wavelength_axis()
        if self.transposed_data is not None:
            self.update_slice_info()

    def _set_spectral_axis(self, wcs, header):
        """Record the file's spectral axis and the unit it states, for a new load.

        A wavelength unit the user chose is kept for a file that states no unit, and for one
        that states the unit the choice was made over: it corrects that header. A file that
        states any other unit clears the choice, and its own unit is used.
        """
        index = spectral_axis(wcs, header) if wcs is not None else None
        self._spectral_index = index
        self._spectral_header_unit = spectral_unit(wcs, header, index)
        self._spectral_stated_unit = stated_unit(header, index)
        self._spectral_scale = header_value_scale(wcs, header, index)
        stated = self._spectral_stated_unit
        if stated is not None and (self._override_over_unit is None
                                   or stated != self._override_over_unit):
            self.wavelength_unit_override = None
            self._override_over_unit = None

    def _sync_timeline_wavelength_axis(self):
        """Show the timeline's wavelength axis for a spectral Z axis, and redraw its ticks.

        A spectral axis whose unit is not a wavelength (a velocity) has none to show; its
        ticks would repeat the channels.
        """
        unit = self.wavelength_unit()
        if self.wcs_z_idx is not None and (unit is None or in_microns(1.0, unit) is not None):
            self.imv.ui.roiPlot.showAxis('top')
        else:
            self.imv.ui.roiPlot.hideAxis('top')
        # The tick strings depend on the unit; the axis caches what it drew
        self.top_axis.picture = None
        self.top_axis.update()

    def get_wavelength_for_slice(self, z):
        """The wavelength of channel `z` as shown (`displayed_wavelength`): in µm for a unit
        the header states, in the header's own numbers for a unit the user chose or an Unknown
        one, and None when Z is not a spectral axis or its unit is not a wavelength, frequency
        or energy."""
        if getattr(self, 'wcs', None) is None or getattr(self, 'wcs_z_idx', None) is None:
            return None
        pixel = [0] * self.wcs.naxis
        pixel[self.wcs_z_idx] = z
        try:
            value = self.wcs.wcs_pix2world([pixel], 0)[0][self.wcs_z_idx]
        except Exception:
            return None
        return self.displayed_wavelength(value)

    def wavelength_text(self, first, last=None):
        """`first` (or the range `first`-`last`) from `get_wavelength_for_slice`, labelled for
        the slice readout: "Wavelength: 2.2005 µm", "Wavelength (Unknown): 19968.7" or
        "Wavelength (Å, set by you): 19968.7"."""
        label = self.wavelength_unit_label()
        in_um = self._shows_stated_microns()
        fmt = "{:.4f}" if in_um else "{:.6g}"
        values = fmt.format(first) if last is None else f"{fmt.format(first)}-{fmt.format(last)}"
        name = "Wavelength" if last is None else "Wavelengths"
        return f"{name}: {values} µm" if in_um else f"{name} ({label}): {values}"

    def clamp_z_range(self, zmin, zmax, write_back=False):
        """Clamp a channel range to the cube and return it in ascending order.

        Returns `(zmin, zmax)`, inclusive, or None if there is no cube. Clamping *both*
        ends matters: a reversed or past-the-end range slices an empty subcube, and the
        nan-reductions then return an all-NaN plane (see B12/B16). With `write_back` the
        corrected values are pushed into the Z Min / Z Max boxes so the UI shows the range
        that was actually used.
        """
        if getattr(self, 'transposed_data', None) is None or self.transposed_data.ndim != 3:
            return None
        nz = self.transposed_data.shape[0]
        zmin = int(np.clip(int(zmin), 0, nz - 1))
        zmax = int(np.clip(int(zmax), 0, nz - 1))
        if zmin > zmax:
            zmin, zmax = zmax, zmin

        if write_back and hasattr(self, 'txt_zmin'):
            # setText() does not re-emit editingFinished, so this cannot recurse
            if self.txt_zmin.text() != str(zmin):
                self.txt_zmin.setText(str(zmin))
            if self.txt_zmax.text() != str(zmax):
                self.txt_zmax.setText(str(zmax))
        return zmin, zmax

    def z_range_from_fields(self, write_back=False):
        """The clamped collapse range in the Z Min / Z Max boxes, or None if unparsable."""
        try:
            zmin = int(self.txt_zmin.text())
            zmax = int(self.txt_zmax.text())
        except (ValueError, AttributeError):
            return None
        return self.clamp_z_range(zmin, zmax, write_back=write_back)

    def z_fields_unparsable(self):
        """True when a cube is loaded and Z Min or Z Max does not hold a whole number.

        The validators keep letters out of what is typed, but `setText` and an emptied box
        bypass them (R84).
        """
        data = getattr(self, 'transposed_data', None)
        return (data is not None and data.ndim == 3
                and self.z_range_from_fields() is None)

    def z_range_in_effect(self, write_back=False):
        """The channel range a Z Range collapse covers: the Z Min / Z Max boxes, or the whole
        cube while either does not parse.

        Everything that draws or reads the collapse asks this, not `z_range_from_fields`, so the
        plane on screen, `display_data`, `current_plane()` and the slice label agree. Stopping at
        an unparsable box left the ImageView's cube painted at channel 0 (R84). A box that does
        not parse is never rewritten.
        """
        rng = self.z_range_from_fields(write_back=write_back)
        if rng is None and self.z_fields_unparsable():
            return self.clamp_z_range(0, self.transposed_data.shape[0] - 1)
        return rng

    def boxcar_width(self):
        """The Boxcar setting, at least 1."""
        try:
            return max(1, int(self.txt_boxcar.text()))
        except (ValueError, AttributeError):
            return 1

    def boxcar_range(self, z=None):
        """The inclusive channel range the Boxcar setting averages around `z`."""
        if z is None:
            z = self.slider_slice.value()
        half = self.boxcar_width() // 2
        return self.clamp_z_range(z - half, z + half)

    def collapse_plane(self, zmin, zmax, method=None):
        """Collapse `transposed_data` over the inclusive range `[zmin, zmax]` into a plane.

        The single definition of the collapse arithmetic, shared by `apply_z_range`,
        `apply_z_slice` (Boxcar) and `current_plane`.
        """
        if getattr(self, 'transposed_data', None) is None or self.transposed_data.ndim != 3:
            return None
        if method is None:
            method = self.combo_collapse.currentText()

        subcube = self.transposed_data[zmin:zmax + 1, :, :]
        if subcube.shape[0] == 0:
            return None  # clamp_z_range makes this unreachable; kept so callers can't blank

        # An all-NaN region is expected for dead slices and is handled downstream by the
        # all-invalid guard in update_image_display; don't spam the console about it.
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            if method == "Median":
                return np.nanmedian(subcube, axis=0)
            if method == "Mean":
                return np.nanmean(subcube, axis=0)
            if method == "Sum":
                return np.nansum(subcube, axis=0)
        return subcube[0]

    def _draw_collapse(self, zmin, zmax, method=None):
        """`collapse_plane`, for the plane about to be drawn; kept for `current_plane`.

        `apply_z_range` and `apply_z_slice` always collapse, so a redraw is never served from an
        older plane, and record what they drew with a key of what produced it. Every open tool
        then reads that plane through `current_plane()` rather than collapsing the cube again:
        seven tools open in Z Range mode used to collapse 465 channels seven times for one
        change. The plane is stored before the flip, the rotations and the DN multiplier, which
        are applied afterwards, so the key does not depend on them.
        """
        method = method or self.combo_collapse.currentText()
        plane = self.collapse_plane(zmin, zmax, method=method)
        self._drawn_collapse = None if plane is None else (
            (self.data_generation, zmin, zmax, method), plane)
        return plane

    def _collapse_for_reading(self, zmin, zmax, method=None):
        """The collapse over `[zmin, zmax]`: the drawn plane if it was made from the same data,
        range and method, otherwise a new collapse."""
        method = method or self.combo_collapse.currentText()
        drawn = getattr(self, '_drawn_collapse', None)
        if drawn is not None and drawn[0] == (self.data_generation, zmin, zmax, method):
            return drawn[1]
        return self.collapse_plane(zmin, zmax, method=method)

    def apply_spatial_transforms(self, arr):
        """Return `arr` with the display flip and 90° rotations applied.

        Pure: it neither touches `display_data` nor applies the DN multiplier. Accepts a
        2-D plane (x, y) or a 3-D cube (z, x, y).
        """
        if arr is None:
            return None
        k = self.rot_angle // 90
        if arr.ndim == 3:
            if self.flip:
                arr = np.flip(arr, axis=1)  # flip X
            if k != 0:
                arr = np.rot90(arr, k=k, axes=(1, 2))
        else:
            if self.flip:
                arr = np.flip(arr, axis=0)  # flip X
            if k != 0:
                arr = np.rot90(arr, k=k)
        return arr

    def orig_spatial_dims(self):
        """`(nx, ny)` of `transposed_data`'s spatial axes, before flip and rotation.

        The last two axes are the spatial ones for both a 2-D image `(x, y)` and a cube
        `(z, x, y)`. Returns None when there is nothing loaded.
        """
        if getattr(self, 'transposed_data', None) is None:
            return None
        nx, ny = self.transposed_data.shape[-2:]
        return int(nx), int(ny)

    # ------------------------------------------------------- exclusive drag handling

    def begin_exclusive_drag(self, owner, handler, on_revoked=None):
        """Give `owner` sole control of the view's drag handling until it gives it back.

        Drawing a box or a region works by replacing `ViewBox.mouseDragEvent`, and only one
        thing can hold it at a time. Each caller used to save the current handler itself and
        restore it on the way out, which corrupts as soon as two of them overlap: the second
        saves the *first's* handler, and whichever finishes last restores the wrong one, leaving
        the view permanently unable to pan. Ownership is tracked here instead, and the previous
        owner is told (`on_revoked`) so it can un-check its own button.
        """
        view = self.imv.getView()
        if self._drag_owner is not None and self._drag_owner is not owner:
            self._revoke_exclusive_drag()

        if self._drag_handler_before is None:
            # Captured once, and only ever the genuine original.
            self._drag_handler_before = view.mouseDragEvent

        view.mouseDragEvent = handler
        view.setMouseEnabled(x=False, y=False)
        self._drag_owner = owner
        self._drag_revoked_callback = on_revoked

    def end_exclusive_drag(self, owner=None):
        """Hand drag handling back. A non-owner asking for this is ignored, not obeyed."""
        if self._drag_owner is None:
            return
        if owner is not None and self._drag_owner is not owner:
            return

        view = self.imv.getView()
        if self._drag_handler_before is not None:
            view.mouseDragEvent = self._drag_handler_before
            self._drag_handler_before = None
        view.setMouseEnabled(x=True, y=True)
        self._drag_owner = None
        self._drag_revoked_callback = None

    def exclusive_drag_owner(self):
        return self._drag_owner

    def _revoke_exclusive_drag(self):
        """Take the drag away from its current owner and let it tidy up its own UI."""
        callback = self._drag_revoked_callback
        self.end_exclusive_drag()
        if callback is not None:
            callback()

    def display_axis_indices(self):
        """The 0-based FITS axis indices currently shown as X and Y.

        For a 2-D image this is `(0, 1)`; for an OSIRIS cube, whose X axis is FITS axis 3, it
        is `(2, 1)`. Anything that has to talk to a WCS or to ds9 needs this — ds9's `image`
        frame always means FITS axes 1 and 2, so a cube displayed on other axes cannot use it.

        The expression was repeated in three places with two different fallbacks, one of which
        (`AXIS 1`) names the wavelength axis for an OSIRIS cube.
        """
        def index_of(attribute, default):
            name = getattr(self, attribute, None) or default
            try:
                return max(0, int(str(name).split()[-1]) - 1)
            except (ValueError, IndexError):
                return int(str(default).split()[-1]) - 1

        naxis = self.raw_data.ndim if getattr(self, 'raw_data', None) is not None else 2
        if naxis < 3:
            # A 2-D image has no axis mapping to consult; X is axis 1 and Y is axis 2.
            return (0, 1)
        return (index_of('current_x_axis', 'AXIS 3'), index_of('current_y_axis', 'AXIS 2'))

    def placement_key(self):
        """Everything that decides where an overlay stored in orig or sky coordinates is drawn on
        the ImageItem: the flip, the 90° rotation, the plane's dimensions, the displayed FITS
        axes, the WCS and the data.

        `display_changed` is also emitted for a unit change, which moves nothing. The region
        layer and the catalog compare this with the key they last placed under and skip the
        re-placement when it is unchanged; it cost 148 ms and 56 ms per unit change. The view
        rotation is not part of it: it is a transform on the ImageItem, which items parented to
        it follow (`view_rotation_changed`).
        """
        return (self.flip, self.rot_angle, self.orig_spatial_dims(), self.display_axis_indices(),
                self.data_generation, id(self.wcs))

    def orig_to_display(self, x, y):
        """Map a `transposed_data` coordinate to its position on screen, or None if no data.

        Thin adapter over `pyql3.core.coords`; see that module for what "orig" means and why
        the arithmetic lives in exactly one place (`BUGS.md` B13/B14).
        """
        dims = self.orig_spatial_dims()
        if dims is None:
            return None
        return coords.orig_to_display(x, y, *dims, flip=self.flip, rot_angle=self.rot_angle)

    def orig_to_display_arrays(self, xs, ys):
        """`orig_to_display` over whole arrays of coordinates, or None if no data.

        For overlays with one position per catalog row (`BUGS.md` R31).
        """
        dims = self.orig_spatial_dims()
        if dims is None:
            return None
        return coords.orig_to_display_arrays(xs, ys, *dims, flip=self.flip,
                                             rot_angle=self.rot_angle)

    def display_to_orig(self, x, y):
        """Map a screen coordinate back to a `transposed_data` coordinate, or None if no data."""
        dims = self.orig_spatial_dims()
        if dims is None:
            return None
        return coords.display_to_orig(x, y, *dims, flip=self.flip, rot_angle=self.rot_angle)

    def current_plane(self):
        """The 2-D plane currently on screen, oriented like `display_data` but *without*
        the DN multiplier folded in.

        Tools that analyse the displayed pixels of a cube must use this rather than
        indexing a single channel: in Boxcar or Z Range mode the screen shows a collapsed
        plane that exists in no single channel of the cube (see B17). Callers that apply
        `data_multiplier` themselves want this; callers that don't can use `display_data`.
        """
        if getattr(self, 'transposed_data', None) is None:
            return None
        if self.transposed_data.ndim != 3:
            return self.apply_spatial_transforms(self.transposed_data)

        # The collapsed plane the viewer drew, when it is still the one these fields describe
        if hasattr(self, 'radio_range') and self.radio_range.isChecked():
            plane = self._collapse_for_reading(*self.z_range_in_effect())
        elif self.boxcar_width() > 1:
            rng = self.boxcar_range()
            plane = (self._collapse_for_reading(*rng, method="Median")
                     if rng is not None else None)
        else:
            plane = self.transposed_data[self.current_z()]

        return self.apply_spatial_transforms(plane)

    def current_z(self):
        """Canonical z index of the plane currently on screen.

        Prefer this over `imv.currentIndex` in tools: the ImageView index is only
        maintained while a single slice is displayed, and goes stale as soon as a boxcar
        or collapse range is drawn through `bypass_imv`.
        """
        if getattr(self, 'transposed_data', None) is None or self.transposed_data.ndim != 3:
            return 0
        nz = self.transposed_data.shape[0]

        if hasattr(self, 'radio_range') and self.radio_range.isChecked():
            # Collapsed plane: report the middle of the range, as the WCS readout does
            rng = self.z_range_in_effect()
            return (rng[0] + rng[1]) // 2

        # Slice mode, boxcar included: the slider is the source of truth
        return int(np.clip(self.slider_slice.value(), 0, nz - 1))

    def on_imv_time_changed(self, ind, _time=None):
        """Mirror a user-driven timeline drag back onto the Z Slice slider.

        Only user interaction should reach here: our own calls into the ImageView are
        wrapped in `_syncing_slice`, because `imv.setImage()` emits a spurious
        sigTimeChanged(0) that would otherwise yank the slider back to slice 0.

        In Z Range mode the ImageView still holds the full cube behind the collapsed plane,
        and a frame change (playback started in Z Slice mode, for example) repaints one
        channel of it. The slider stays where it is and the collapse is drawn again (R27).
        The frame keys themselves are ignored in this mode; see `eventFilter`.
        """
        if self._syncing_slice or getattr(self, 'transposed_data', None) is None:
            return
        if self.transposed_data.ndim != 3:
            return
        if self.radio_range.isChecked():
            self.apply_z_range()
            return

        try:
            ind = int(ind)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return

        self._syncing_slice = True
        try:
            if self.slider_slice.value() != ind:
                # Drives lbl_slice_val, update_slice_info, the readouts and the tools
                self.slider_slice.setValue(ind)
            else:
                self.update_slice_info()
        finally:
            self._syncing_slice = False

    def eventFilter(self, obj, event):
        """Keep the ImageView's frame keys from painting a channel over a collapse (R27).

        `ImageView.keyPressEvent` repaints a channel of the cube it holds even when the frame
        does not change (Home at frame 0, End at the last frame), and then emits no
        sigTimeChanged, so `on_imv_time_changed` cannot put the collapse back.

        In Z Range mode the presses are ignored: the Z Slice slider is disabled, so the keys
        have nothing to move. In Boxcar mode the stepping keys move the slider instead
        (`_boxcar_key_target`), which draws the median for the new centre; Space, Up and Down,
        which start playback, still reach pyqtgraph: each frame they step comes back through
        `on_imv_time_changed`, and `_after_playback_tick` handles the ticks at either end of
        the cube, which step no frame.

        Only the press is handled here. The release has to reach pyqtgraph: it removes the key
        from `keysPressed` and stops playback, and a key pressed in Z Slice mode and released
        here would otherwise stay pressed and resume playback later.
        """
        if obj is self.imv and event.type() == QEvent.KeyPress and event.key() in _FRAME_KEYS:
            if self.radio_range.isChecked():
                event.accept()
                return True
            target = self._boxcar_key_target(event.key())
            if target is not None:
                self.slider_slice.setValue(target)
                event.accept()
                return True
        return super().eventFilter(obj, event)

    def _after_playback_tick(self):
        """Stop a Boxcar playback that has reached the end of the cube, and redraw the median.

        pyqtgraph does not stop playback at the first or last frame: each further tick sets
        the frame it is already on, which repaints that raw channel and emits no
        sigTimeChanged, so `on_imv_time_changed` never hears of it.
        """
        if getattr(self, 'transposed_data', None) is None or self.transposed_data.ndim != 3:
            return
        if self.radio_range.isChecked() or self.boxcar_width() <= 1:
            return
        index = self.imv.currentIndex
        last = self.imv.nframes() - 1
        if 0 < index < last:
            return
        # pyqtgraph may already have set the rate to 0 in this tick, before its last repaint
        rate = self.imv.playRate or 0
        if (rate > 0 and index >= last) or (rate < 0 and index <= 0):
            self.imv.play(0)
        self.update_image_display(bypass_imv=True)

    def _boxcar_key_target(self, key):
        """The slider value a frame key moves to in Boxcar mode, or None when the key is
        not a stepping key or Boxcar is off. Clamped to the slider's range."""
        if getattr(self, 'transposed_data', None) is None or self.transposed_data.ndim != 3:
            return None
        if self.boxcar_width() <= 1:
            return None
        slider = self.slider_slice
        value = slider.value()
        targets = {
            Qt.Key_Home: slider.minimum(),
            Qt.Key_End: slider.maximum(),
            Qt.Key_Left: value - 1,
            Qt.Key_Right: value + 1,
            Qt.Key_PageUp: value - slider.pageStep(),
            Qt.Key_PageDown: value + slider.pageStep(),
        }
        if key not in targets:
            return None
        return int(np.clip(targets[key], slider.minimum(), slider.maximum()))

    def refresh_plane_validity(self):
        """Recompute whether the plane on screen has any finite pixel at all.

        Cheap (one plane, never the whole cube) and has to be re-run on every slice change:
        paging onto a dead channel does not redisplay the image, it only moves the
        ImageView's index.
        """
        data = getattr(self, 'display_data', None)
        if data is None:
            self._plane_all_invalid = False
            return self._plane_all_invalid
        plane = data
        if plane.ndim == 3:
            plane = plane[int(np.clip(self.current_z(), 0, plane.shape[0] - 1))]
        self._plane_all_invalid = not bool(np.isfinite(plane).any())
        return self._plane_all_invalid

    def update_slice_info(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self._update_slice_info_text()
        # An all-invalid plane otherwise looks identical to a display bug (see B16)
        if self.refresh_plane_validity() and hasattr(self, 'lbl_slice_info'):
            self.lbl_slice_info.setText(self.lbl_slice_info.text() + "  —  no valid data")

    def _update_slice_info_text(self):
        if getattr(self, 'transposed_data', None) is None:
            if hasattr(self, 'lbl_slice_info'):
                self.lbl_slice_info.setText("Slice: N/A")
            return

        if hasattr(self, 'radio_range') and self.radio_range.isChecked():
            rng = self.z_range_in_effect()
            if rng is None:
                self.lbl_slice_info.setText("Collapsed: Invalid Range")
            else:
                zmin, zmax = rng
                text = f"Collapsed: {zmin}-{zmax}"

                wave_min = self.get_wavelength_for_slice(zmin)
                wave_max = self.get_wavelength_for_slice(zmax)
                if wave_min is not None and wave_max is not None:
                    text += f", {self.wavelength_text(wave_min, wave_max)}"
                if self.z_fields_unparsable():
                    text += "  —  Invalid Range in Z Min/Z Max, full range used"

                else:
                    text = f"Slice: {z}"
                    wave = self.get_wavelength_for_slice(z)
                    if wave is not None:
                        text += f", {self.wavelength_text(wave)}"

                self.lbl_slice_info.setText(text)
            else:

    def _custom_tickStrings(self, values, scale, spacing):
        if self.wcs is None or self.wcs_z_idx is None:
            return self._original_tickStrings(values, scale, spacing)

        known = self._shows_stated_microns()
        strings = []
        for val in values:
            if val < 0:
                strings.append("")
                continue
            wave = self.get_wavelength_for_slice(val)
            if wave is None:
                strings.append(str(val))
            else:
                strings.append(f"{wave:.4f} µm" if known else f"{wave:.6g}")
        return strings

        self.imv.getView().setAspectLocked(True)

    def main_zoom_in(self):

    def main_zoom_11(self):
        """One data pixel per screen pixel, centred where the view is now (R66).

        The range is the ViewBox's size in screen pixels, in data units: the ImageItem is one
        unit per pixel, whatever the view rotation. Setting it to the whole image, as this did,
        is Fit."""
        self.imv.getView().setAspectLocked(True)
        if self.display_data is not None:
            self._set_one_to_one(x=True, y=True)

    def _set_one_to_one(self, x, y):
        """Make the chosen axes span the ViewBox's screen size, about the current centre.
        Falls back to the whole image on an axis when the ViewBox has no size yet."""
        view = self.imv.getView()
        rect = view.viewRect()
        w, h = self.display_data.shape[-2:]
        ranges = {}
        for key, wanted, screen, centre, extent in (
                ('xRange', x, view.width(), rect.center().x(), w),
                ('yRange', y, view.height(), rect.center().y(), h)):
            if not wanted:
                continue
            if screen > 0:
                ranges[key] = (centre - screen / 2.0, centre + screen / 2.0)
            else:
                ranges[key] = (0, extent)
        view.setRange(padding=0, **ranges)

    def independent_zoom(self, x=None, y=None):
